meta.topic: Outside coverage of Anthropic, PBC S-1/A Amendment No. 1 (accession 0001628280-26-068676, filed 2026-11-02)
meta.scope_note: Outside news and commentary only; the filing itself was not read for this file. Figures are as reported by outlets and should be reconciled against the filing by the filing-reading process.
meta.headline_finding: Amendment No. 1 contains NO price range, NO share count and NO offering size (all still blank per Yahoo Finance, TechTimes, Stocktwits, Data Studios). Its news is Q3 2026 results, the ~$895.4B commitments total, and named retail platforms. Valuation and timing figures in circulation come from press reporting (WSJ, Reuters, Bloomberg), not the filing.

reliability_legend.direct: Read on the original outlet's page (or wire copy carrying the wire's credit).
reliability_legend.syndicated: Read on a syndication partner (e.g. Yahoo Finance, MarketScreener) carrying the original byline.
reliability_legend.secondhand: Original is paywalled or not reached; content taken from another outlet's summary. Both outlets named.
reliability_legend.headline_only: Only headline / search snippet seen; content not verified.
reliability_legend.primary_other: Read in another company's SEC filing (not the Anthropic filing).

reported_terms.value: WSJ: $1.5T-$1.6T; Reuters: ~$1.5T; Bloomberg: $1.4T-$1.5T; earlier talk ~$2T; last private round $965B (May 2026)
reported_terms.detail: WSJ (Nov 2): institutional investors advised Anthropic and its advisers over the past several days to price at ~$1.5-1.6T, citing last week's tech selloff, AI overexposure, data-center political backlash, hyperscaler AI-profit uncertainty. Some investors expect CFO Krishna Rao to price conservatively; some believe a debut near $1.5T could rise toward $2T by end of first session. Reuters (Nov 2) repeats that some investors are weighing ~$1.5T (originally reported Oct 15). Bloomberg (per TNW): investors discussed $1.4T-$1.5T. Nasdaq Private Market latest private mark $1.41T (per Stocktwits).

reported_terms.detail: Yahoo chart breakdown: Broadcom $161.2B (equipment leases); Google $121.3B (up from $114.5B in first filing); SpaceX AI unit up to $120.5B; Amazon $110.0B; Microsoft $44.9B; Nscale up to $44.6B; Lambda $41.3B. Not in total: planned $125-150B of Google chips and >$20B with AMD (no fixed dollar commitment). Purchase commitments ~$314B vs $55B at end-2025. Cape Fear Advisors (via TechTimes) says $213.8B is conditional/terminable. WSJ (via Stocktwits): above the ~$800B analysts had gathered from the draft. context.topic: Index moves Nov 3 (Tue, US midterm election day) - intraday
context.detail: Early trade: Nasdaq +0.4% to +0.8% (sources vary), S&P +0.19%, Dow lower on Apple (-3% to -3.5%). Chip rebound: Nvidia +3.3%, AMD +4.6% ahead of earnings, Intel +3.2%. Palantir -4.2%. Morgan Stanley analysts said correction 'may be nearing its final stages' (per Invezz). Not a close.

Revenue $127.6B; operating income $40.6B; net income $26.5B; diluted EPS $2.12; Google Cloud $30.7B; capex $51.4B (2026 guide $195-205B unchanged; 'significantly' higher in 2027). OI&E -$8.2B; loss on equity securities -$8.66B, 'primarily' unrealized loss on SpaceX after its share price fell in Q3 (CFO). 10-Q: gross unrealized gain on non-marketable equity securities only $3.39B in Q3 2026 (vs $10.58B Q3 2025; $117.2B for 9M 2026); non-marketable equity carrying value $128.2B 'primarily' one private company (Alphabet does not name it; widely reported as Anthropic); $20.0B contingent future funding commitment to 'a private company' through 2030. SpaceX holding $75.2B subject to short-term sale restrictions. Shares -10.4% after hours; Oct 29 was described as Alphabet's worst day, losing nearly $500B of market value (The National). Alphabet also priced a EUR 6B multi-tranche bond on Nov 2 (SEC FWP).
context.source: Alphabet 8-K Ex.99.1; Alphabet 10-Q; Investing.com call transcript; The National; Alphabet FWP

context.detail: EPS $1.89 vs $1.96 est.; revenue $201.94B vs $202.31B est.; AWS $45.98B (+39%); net income $20.69B (down y/y because Q3 2025 had a $9.5B pre-tax Anthropic gain); capex $77.3B; TTM FCF -$42.4B; Q4 revenue guide $240-247B; shares -6% after hours, closed -1.41% Oct 30. 10-Q: essentially NO Anthropic income-statement gain in Q3 2026 (total 'upward adjustments relating to equity investments in private companies' $39M; total OI&E -$703M) vs $62.8B of upward adjustments to Anthropic preferred for 9M 2026. At Sept 30: Anthropic non-voting preferred carried at ~$92.5B (164M shares, each convertible into 10 non-voting common); convertible notes fair value ~$146.2B with $140.3B unrealized gain sitting in AOCI (not net income); notes would convert to ~184M preferred absent the 12% ownership cap; at IPO notes convert to unregistered Class N non-voting common, subject to cap; Amazon expects a customary lock-up. $20B Anthropic financing facility ($15B remaining) expires 30 months after IPO.

FT (Oct 30, via Reuters/Investing.com, published Nov 2): OpenAI cut its funding-round target by ~$10B to ~$20B and lowered desired valuation to $1.25T from $1.4T amid tech rout; UAE consortium incl. MGX expected largest participant; Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia, a16z expected; later retail offering planned at $1.25T; still pursuing a 2027 listing; wants to close ahead of 'Anthropic's imminent listing'. OpenAI confidentially filed in June 2026; CFO Friar told staff (Aug) it 'will be a public company in 2027'.

Priced $135 (June 11), listed Nasdaq June 12; ~$1.75T-$1.77T valuation at IPO; first-day close $161 (+19%). Peak: ~$211 (Wikipedia) / 52-week intraday high $225.64 (Motley Fool quote widget). Low close $108.27 in early August (CNBC); 52-week intraday low $104.83. Back above $135 by early October. Nov 2 close ~$136.37 (derived: Nov 3 10:46 ET quote $141.65, +$5.28/+3.87%). Market cap ~$1.85T (Fool widget). Alphabet booked a Q3 unrealized loss on SpaceX. Nasdaq-100 fast entry 15 trading days after IPO (joined July 7); not in S&P 500.
context.source: Wikipedia; CNBC (Ashley Capoot); Motley Fool quote page

context.detail: Nasdaq-100 fast-entry rule (since May 1): large new listing can join after 15 trading days if its full market value ranks within the index's top 40 (SpaceX precedent). S&P Dow Jones kept standard rules: 12-month seasoning, four consecutive quarters of positive GAAP earnings, minimum float - Anthropic's GAAP net losses (Q3 -$23.3B) would currently block S&P 500 eligibility; one estimate puts earliest S&P 500 entry at late 2027. FTSE Russell has a ~5-trading-day fast entry.
context.reliability: direct for headline facts (ETF Stream not fetched)

context.detail: KBRA assigned BB+ (highest junk tier) in June 2026, reported mid-Oct by FT. FT (Oct 30, via TechCrunch): Blackstone, anchor of a $63B chip-financing deal, told investors it expects a double-B-range rating after IPO, reversing an earlier investment-grade-before-2027 view.
